content:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE - high 5xx / connreset spike observed from ALB in euc4b at 2026-03-15T04:12Z. Paging euc4 on-call. Please ack and triage. :rotating_light:

sam: Acked. I'm on it. Seeing alerts from infra-monitor: backend_5xx_rate + connreset_rate both up around 07:12 UTC.

priya: Confirming. CloudWatch: TargetGroup arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/redwood-app-tg-euc4b showing healthy_count flipping between 1 and 4 every ~30s. HealthCheck[HTTP:/healthz] failing with 504/connection reset on some targets.

mike: Noticed recent deploy to eu cluster in euc4b ~03:55 UTC. Could be new image, but metric spike lines up with ALB target oscillation, not app CPU. Rolling back only if we see app-level errors.

sam: Pulling target health now.

sam: ```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/redwood-app-tg-euc4b
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    { "Target": {"Id":"10.0.12.45"}, "TargetHealth": {"State":"unhealthy","Reason":"Target.ResponseCodeMismatch"}},
    { "Target": {"Id":"10.0.12.46"}, "TargetHealth": {"State":"healthy"}},
    { "Target": {"Id":"10.0.12.47"}, "TargetHealth": {"State":"initial"}}
  ]
}
```

priya: That ResponseCodeMismatch is odd — our healthz returns 200 quickly when I curl the pod from cluster network. Could be intermittent networking (socket resets) between ALB and nodeport/ingress.

dmitri: On the ingress side, envoy logs show upstream reset ECONNRESET to pods on ip 10.0.12.45 around same timestamp. Example from envoy: ``[warning] upstream_reset: connection reset by peer, downstream 502``.

jess: Customer impact check: edge-proxy metrics show 6-9% request 5xx increase for requests routed to euc4b for the last 6m. No global outage. Affected: hosted-api customers with region affinity set to euc4. Notifying SRE lead and CS.

opsbot: Notifying status page: "Partial degradation in euc4 region for API requests. Investigating." :white_circle:

sam: Immediate mitigation idea: remove problematic AZ targets from ALB target group to stop oscillation and let traffic drain to other AZs. We can do a dynamic modify-target-group-attributes or deregister specific targets. Thoughts?

mike: +1. If we remove the targets in euc4b zone temporarily, will shift traffic to healthy AZs and avoid retries causing 502s. Need to watch capacity. Also consider increasing ALB deregistration delay to allow graceful drain.

priya: I'll deregister ip 10.0.12.45 and 10.0.12.47 from the TG and mark manual drained. Doing now.

priya: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=10.0.12.45 Id=10.0.12.47```

sam: After deregister: healthy_count stabilized to 3, 5xx rate back down to baseline in 90s. Observability shows connection reset traces drop to normal.

jess: Good. Assigning incident severity: sev2 (partial degraded). Notifying top impacted customers via CS with ETA for mitigation: traffic shifted, continuing investigation into root cause.

dmitri: Root cause hypotheses: (1) kernel-level conntrack exhaustion on nodes serving those targets, (2) ingress controller bug causing connection resets under specific request pattern, (3) underlying NIC flapping in that AZ. Need deeper node metrics and kubelet logs.

mike: I'm grabbing node-level logs and sysstat. Also checking recent AMI/driver updates in the node pool.

priya: I'll re-run healthchecks against pods through node port from ALB subnet to reproduce. If we can't immediately find root cause, plan: keep targets deregistered, schedule a rolling restart of the problematic node pool tomorrow with safe window, and consider a permanent weight shift away from euc4b until we validate infra.

sam: On-call handoff: I'm taking lead for active mitigation until 06:00 UTC, then jess will take over for postmortem follow-up and customer comms.

jess: Acknowledged. I'll coordinate post-incident writeup and include timeline, mitigations (deregistered targets), customer impact numbers, and next steps.

oncall-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated (partial), lead=sam, next_handoff=2339007000. Please update incident bridge if anything changes.

mike: Recording investigation note: collect /var/log/kern.log, `ss -s`, dmesg for nodes 10.0.12.45/47 and ALB access logs for full request traces.

jess: Copy. CS notified customers with affected requests <10%. Will keep status page updated.

priya: Leaving a sticky: if we see tg health oscillations again, consider switching ALB health check to TCP for short term to reduce app-level variance.

sam: Closing active paging for now. We'll keep thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
